edition.locus: Baehrens GCS 33 Comm. Cant. Liber II 5

source_text: Equitatui meo in curribus Pharaonis assimilavi te, amica mea. Quantum distat equitatus Domini ab equis Pharaonis, tantum ecclesia a filiabus alienis. Genae tuae sicut turturis; collum tuum sicut monilia: simplicitas et obedientia ornatus animae. Murenulas aureas faciemus tibi vermiculatas argento, donec rex in accubitu suo est: amici sponsi interim ornamenta praeparant.
pass_a_gloss: To-cavalry my in chariots of-Pharaoh I-likened you, friend my. By-as-much-as differs cavalry of-Lord from horses of-Pharaoh...
pass_b_english: [[I have likened you, my friend, to my cavalry among Pharaoh’s chariots >> Bible:Song of Songs 1:9]]. As far as the Lord’s cavalry differs from Pharaoh’s horses, so far the church from alien daughters. [[Your cheeks are like a turtledove’s; your neck like necklaces >> Bible:Song of Songs 1:10]]. Simplicity and obedience are the soul’s adornment. [[We will make you ornaments of gold studded with silver, while the king is on his couch >> Bible:Song of Songs 1:11-12]]: the Bridegroom’s friends prepare ornaments for a time.
